comments.text: Tutuila is one of those places most people have never heard of, yet its story is incredible. 🌊 With the island slowly sinking, would you choose to stay and protect your family's homeland or leave for a safer future? replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: @TiaoaliiLutu Not quite my imagination 😄 NASA actually measured Tutuila sinking by an average of 6-9 mm per year between 2015 and 2022, following the 2009 earthquake. It's called land subsidence. That doesn't mean the entire island is about to disappear, but it does increase the risk of coastal flooding. Here's the NASA study if you're curious: https://www.nasa.gov/centers-and-facilities/goddard/nasa-researchers-measure-sinking-land-in-american-samoa/

comments.text: This documentary is false.Tutuila (American Samoa) is not sinking!Its a large volcanic island. The island atolls of Solomons, Tuvalu and Kiribati are truly sinking or being claimed by rising sea levels!Other parts about this island being beautiful and being untouched is true.

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text:
You're right that Tutuila is a large volcanic island, but volcanic islands can experience land subsidence too. NASA actually measured Tutuila sinking by an average of 6-9mm per year between 2015 and 2022, following the 2009 earthquake. That doesn't mean the entire island is about to disappear underwater, but it does increase the risk of coastal flooding. Here's the NASA research if you'd like to take a look. And I''m glad you appreciated the other parts of the documentary! 🇦🇸❤️
https://www.nasa.gov/centers-and-facilities/goddard/nasa-researchers-measure-sinking-land-in-american-samoa/
